Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEJ502 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Rankine Thermal Efficiency: $\eta = \frac{W_{\text{net}}}{Q_{\text{in}}} = \frac{(h_1 - h_2) - (h_4 - h_3)}{h_1 - h_4}$
  • Reheat Cycle Purpose: Prevents excessive moisture at turbine exhaust (keeps dryness fraction $x > 0.88$) and increases cycle thermal efficiency.
  • Regenerative Feedwater Heating: Bleeds steam from turbine stages to preheat boiler feed water, raising mean temperature of heat addition ($\bar{T}_{in}$).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Pump Work Neglect: $W_p = v_f (p_{\text{boiler}} - p_{\text{condenser}})$, typically small (<1.5% of turbine work).
  • Supercritical Power Cycles: Operate above 22.1 MPa where water turns directly into steam without boiling interface.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Reheating increases specific work output significantly and increases thermal efficiency moderately.
  • Condenser vacuum must be maintained near 0.05-0.08 bar absolute for high efficiency.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Vapour Power Cycles & Modern Steam Stations

1. Modern Reheat & Regenerative Station Thermals

Thermal efficiency increases as the Carnot mean temperature of heat addition approaches peak cycle temperature. Superheating, intermediate pressure reheating, and multi-stage open/closed feedwater heaters optimize thermodynamic conversion.

$$\bar{T}_{\text{in}} = \frac{q_{\text{in}}}{\Delta s}, \quad \eta_{\text{th}} = 1 - \frac{T_{\text{condenser}}}{\bar{T}_{\text{in}}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Supercritical coal-fired thermal power stations and nuclear steam turbine power plants.

Module 2.title: Vapour Compression Refrigeration Systems (VCRS)
Module 2.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 150" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">VCRS Cycle on P-h Diagram</text>
  <path d="M 80 120 L 180 50 L 320 50 L 80 120" fill="none" stroke="#10b981" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <text x="90" y="75" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="10">Condenser</text><text x="90" y="135" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="10">Evaporator</text>
  <text x="220" y="130" fill="#cbd5e1" font-size="11">COP = (h1 - h4) / (h2 - h1) [Refrigerating Effect / Work]</text>
</svg>
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEJ502 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Coefficient of Performance (COP): $COP = \frac{\text{Refrigerating Effect}}{\text{Compressor Work}} = \frac{h_1 - h_4}{h_2 - h_1}$
  • 1 Ton of Refrigeration (TR): $1 \text{ TR} = 3.517 \text{ kW} = 210 \text{ kJ/min}$ (Heat rate to freeze 1 ton of water at 0°C in 24 hrs)
  • Isenthalpic Throttling: $h_3 = h_4$ (across capillary tube or thermostatic expansion valve)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Subcooling vs Superheating: Subcooling liquid leaves condenser below saturation, increasing refrigerating effect without increasing compressor work; Superheating ensures dry vapour enters compressor.
  • Eco-Refrigerants: Transition from CFCs/HCFCs (R12, R22) to low-GWP hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs like R1234yf) and natural refrigerants ($CO_2, NH_3$).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Expansion process is isenthalpic ($h_3 = h_4$), NOT isentropic.
  • Theoretical COP of Carnot refrigerator: $COP_{\text{Carnot}} = \frac{T_L}{T_H - T_L}$.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Refrigeration Thermodynamics & Component Sizing

1. Vapour Compression Thermodynamic State Analysis

Four thermodynamic processes: Isentropic compression (1-2), isobaric heat rejection in condenser (2-3), isenthalpic throttling expansion (3-4), and isobaric heat absorption in evaporator (4-1).

$$W_c = \dot{m}(h_2 - h_1), \quad Q_e = \dot{m}(h_1 - h_4), \quad COP = \frac{h_1 - h_4}{h_2 - h_1}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Cold storage logistics, domestic inverter refrigerators, and industrial process chillers.

Module 3.title: Psychrometry & Air Conditioning Processes
Module 3.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 150" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Psychrometric Processes (Sensible vs Latent)</text>
  <line x1="100" y1="100" x2="300" y2="100" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="3"/>
  <text x="140" y="90" fill="#ef4444" font-size="10">Sensible Heating</text>
  <line x1="200" y1="100" x2="200" y2="40" stroke="#38bdf8" stroke-width="3"/>
  <text x="210" y="65" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="10">Humidification</text>
  <text x="130" y="135" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="11">RSHF = Sensible Heat / (Sensible + Latent Heat)</text>
</svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEJ502 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Specific Humidity / Humidity Ratio ($\omega$): $\omega = 0.622 \frac{p_v}{p_a - p_v} = 0.622 \frac{p_v}{p_t - p_v}$ (kg water / kg dry air)
  • Relative Humidity ($\phi$): $\phi = \frac{p_v}{p_{vs}}$ (Ratio of actual partial pressure to saturation pressure at same DBT)
  • Sensible Heat Factor (SHF): $SHF = \frac{RSH}{RSH + RLH} = \frac{Q_s}{Q_s + Q_l}$
  • Cooling & Dehumidification: Air passed over cooling coil below dew point temperature ($ADP < DPT$).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Key Temperatures: Dry Bulb Temp (DBT), Wet Bulb Temp (WBT, sling psychrometer), Dew Point Temp (DPT, condensation begins).
  • Bypass Factor ($BF$): $BF = \frac{T_{\text{out}} - T_{\text{coil}}}{T_{\text{in}} - T_{\text{coil}}}$, Coil contact factor $\eta = 1 - BF$.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • At 100% relative humidity (saturation), $DBT = WBT = DPT$.
  • Sensible heating/cooling alters DBT while keeping specific humidity $\omega$ strictly constant.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Psychrometric Formulations & HVAC Sizing

1. Moist Air Thermodynamics & Coil Selection

Applying Dalton's law of partial pressures ($p_t = p_a + p_v$) and psychrometric mass-energy balances allows calculation of required apparatus dew point (ADP) and volumetric airflow CFM.

$$Q_s = 1.005 \dot{m}_a (T_1 - T_2), \quad Q_l = \dot{m}_a h_{fg} (\omega_1 - \omega_2), \quad \dot{V} = \frac{Q_s}{1.08 \Delta T} \text{ (CFM)}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Cleanrooms for semiconductor manufacturing, hospital operating theater HVAC, and commercial malls.

Module 4.title: Gas Turbine Brayton Cycle: Intercooling, Reheat & Regeneration
Module 4.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 150" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Brayton Cycle on T-s Diagram</text>
  <path d="M 120 120 L 160 80 L 300 30 L 350 100 Z" fill="none" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <text x="180" y="45" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="10">Combustor (q_in)</text>
  <text x="140" y="135" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="11">η_th = 1 - 1 / (r_p)^((γ-1)/γ) • Max work: (r_p)_opt = (T3/T1)^(γ/(2(γ-1)))</text>
</svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEJ502 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Brayton Thermal Efficiency: $\eta_{\text{Brayton}} = 1 - \frac{1}{r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma}}$ (where $r_p = p_2/p_1$ is pressure ratio)
  • Optimum Pressure Ratio for Max Work: $(r_p)_{\text{opt}} = \left( \frac{T_{\max}}{T_{\min}} \right)^{\frac{\gamma}{2(\gamma-1)}}$
  • Back Work Ratio ($BWR$): $BWR = \frac{W_{\text{compressor}}}{W_{\text{turbine}}}$ (High: 40-60% in gas turbines, vs <1% in steam turbines)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Cycle Modifications: Intercooling reduces compressor work; Reheating increases turbine work; Regeneration utilizes exhaust waste heat to preheat combustor air.
  • Combined Cycle Power Plant (CCPP): Gas turbine topping cycle + Heat Recovery Steam Generator (HRSG) + Steam turbine bottoming cycle yields >60% thermal efficiency.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Regeneration is only beneficial at low pressure ratios where turbine exhaust is hotter than compressor discharge ($T_4 > T_2$).
  • Turbine entry temperature (TET) is limited by metallurgical creep limits of nickel superalloy blades.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Gas Turbine Mechanics & Combined Cycles

1. Aerodynamic & Thermal Optimization of Gas Turbines

Gas turbines operate on steady-flow open Brayton cycle. Component isentropic efficiencies for compressor ($\eta_c$) and turbine ($\eta_t$) drastically affect net output work.

$$W_{\text{net}} = c_p [ (T_3 - T_4) - (T_2 - T_1) ], \quad \eta_{\text{reg}} = 1 - \left(\frac{T_1}{T_3}\right) r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Aviation turbofan jet engines (Boeing 787/Airbus A350) and CCPP base-load electrical generation stations.

Module 5.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 150" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Convergent-Divergent (de Laval) Supersonic Nozzle</text>
  <polygon points="80,50 180,75 280,40 280,110 180,75 80,100" fill="#1e293b" stroke="#38bdf8" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="165" y="65" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="10">Throat (M=1)</text>
  <text x="90" y="80" fill="#cbd5e1" font-size="10">Subsonic</text><text x="220" y="80" fill="#ef4444" font-size="10">Supersonic (M>1)</text>
</svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEJ502 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Critical Pressure Ratio (Choking): $\frac{p^*}{p_0} = \left( \frac{2}{\gamma + 1} \right)^{\frac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1}}$ ($0.528$ for air $\gamma=1.4$; $0.546$ for superheated steam $\gamma=1.3$)
  • Mach Number & Area Velocity Relation: $\frac{dA}{A} = (M^2 - 1) \frac{dV}{V}$
  • Blade Speed Ratio ($\rho$): Impulse turbine optimum $\rho = \frac{u}{V_1} = \frac{\cos\alpha}{2}$; Reaction turbine (50% Parson's) $\rho = \cos\alpha$
  • Maximum Impulse Blading Efficiency: $\eta_{b,\max} = \cos^2\alpha$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Compounding Methods: Velocity compounding (Curtis stage: single nozzle stage, alternating moving and fixed guide blades); Pressure compounding (Rateau stage: multi-stage nozzles).
  • Degree of Reaction ($R$): $R = \frac{\text{Static enthalpy drop in rotor blades}}{\text{Total enthalpy drop in stage}}$.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • At throat, Mach number is strictly $M=1$ (sonic velocity) when nozzle is choked.
  • Impulse blades experience zero static pressure drop across moving blades; reaction blades experience continuous expansion.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Turbine Gas Dynamics & Velocity Triangles

1. 1D Compressible Nozzle Flow & Velocity Triangles

Expansion of high-pressure fluid through converging-diverging nozzle accelerates flow to supersonic speeds. The resulting kinetic jet deflects over aerofoil blading, generating torque via Euler's turbine equation.

$$P = \dot{m} u (V_{w1} + V_{w2}), \quad \eta_{\text{blade}} = \frac{2 u (V_{w1} + V_{w2})}{V_1^2}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Steam turbine high-pressure cylinders and aerospace liquid rocket exhaust nozzles.
